checks.title: COPPA scope and audience classification
runtime_tests: Where mixed-audience treatment is relied on, exercise the age-screen path with synthetic users and verify personal information is not collected before age information or another permitted age-determination method except as allowed by the Rule.
checks.verify: Review the amended COPPA Rule, including child-directed, mixed-audience and actual-knowledge triggers. Do not infer COPPA merely from the presence or absence of an age field.

checks.title: COPPA parental notice and verifiable parental consent
runtime_tests: Using synthetic child/parent accounts, verify direct notice, online notice, verifiable parental consent before covered collection/use/disclosure, and any relied-on consent exception.
checks.verify: Review 16 CFR Part 312 as amended in 2025, including notice and verifiable-parental-consent requirements and exceptions.

checks.title: COPPA third-party disclosure and targeted-advertising consent
runtime_tests: Trace child-data disclosures and advertising/monetisation flows with synthetic data; where separate parental opt-in is required for third-party disclosure/targeted advertising, verify that flow independently from collection consent.
checks.verify: Review the amended COPPA Rule's third-party disclosure and advertising-consent provisions. Do not assume one parental consent covers every disclosure purpose.

checks.title: COPPA parental review, deletion and further-use controls
runtime_tests: Exercise synthetic parent access/review, deletion and stop-further-use/collection flows; verify authentication and downstream propagation.
checks.verify: Review amended COPPA parental rights and operator obligations for review, deletion and preventing further use or collection.

checks.title: COPPA security, retention and deletion program
runtime_tests: Inspect child-data access controls and retention schedules; verify deletion when information is no longer reasonably necessary and test representative processor/downstream deletion behavior where feasible.
checks.verify: Review amended COPPA security, retention and deletion requirements, including the requirement for a written data-retention policy/program where applicable.

checks.title: CAN-SPAM commercial email
runtime_tests: Send test commercial email and verify non-deceptive header/subject information, sender identification, postal address, clear opt-out, functioning opt-out processing and persistent suppression.
checks.verify: Classify the message's primary purpose under CAN-SPAM/16 CFR Part 316. B2B commercial email is not categorically exempt; transactional/relationship messages have different treatment.

checks.title: DMCA §512(c) safe-harbor role and baseline conditions
checks.verify: Determine whether the service stores material at the direction of users and seeks §512(c) safe-harbor protection. Registration alone does not establish safe-harbor eligibility.

checks.title: DMCA designated agent registration and publication
runtime_tests: Verify the publicly accessible designated-agent contact matches the current Copyright Office electronic directory record.
checks.verify: Review 17 U.S.C. §512(c)(2) and 37 CFR §201.38. Keep the website and Copyright Office agent information current and accurate.

checks.title: DMCA notice, takedown and counter-notice workflow
runtime_tests: Run a synthetic notice/counter-notice tabletop; verify intake, required-field review, expeditious removal/disablement decision path, user notification, counter-notice handling and restoration timing where applicable.
checks.verify: Review §512(c), (g) and current Copyright Office materials. Beacon does not determine whether a work is infringing.

checks.title: DMCA repeat-infringer policy and standard technical measures
runtime_tests: Using synthetic account history, verify the repeat-infringer policy can be applied in appropriate circumstances and that account/action records are retained consistently.
checks.verify: Review §512(i) and current case-law-sensitive guidance. Do not equate one complaint with a legal finding of infringement.

checks.title: ADA Title III web accessibility for public accommodations
runtime_tests: Run automated accessibility checks plus keyboard, focus, zoom, screen-reader and error-message tests on representative public-facing flows. Treat WCAG as useful technical guidance rather than an automatic Title III legal verdict.
checks.verify: Review DOJ ADA web-accessibility guidance and current binding law for the business/jurisdiction. DOJ guidance states that businesses open to the public must provide accessible online goods/services, while Title III lacks the same specific federal web technical rule that applies to Title II.

checks.title: ADA Title II web/mobile accessibility — public entities 50,000+
runtime_tests: Test representative web/mobile content against WCAG 2.1 Level AA and the Title II rule's scope/exceptions; include manual keyboard and screen-reader review.
checks.verify: Review DOJ Title II web/mobile rule and the 2026 interim final rule extending the compliance date for public entities with population 50,000 or more to 26 April 2027.

checks.title: ADA Title II web/mobile accessibility — smaller public entities and special districts
runtime_tests: Test representative web/mobile content against WCAG 2.1 Level AA and the Title II rule's scope/exceptions; include manual keyboard and screen-reader review.
checks.verify: Review DOJ Title II web/mobile rule and the 2026 interim final rule extending the compliance date for public entities under 50,000 population or special district governments to 26 April 2028.

limitations: This pack covers selected federal digital-product regimes only; it does not cover state privacy, consumer-protection, biometric, health, employment, accessibility or marketing laws.
COPPA applicability depends on audience, actual knowledge and collection of personal information; age-screen design is fact-specific.
DMCA §512 is a conditional limitation on liability, not a certification that user content is lawful.
ADA Title III web-accessibility obligations and remedies can depend on binding law in the relevant jurisdiction; Beacon does not convert WCAG test results directly into legal violations.
A PASS reflects the supplied evidence contract for the modeled check, not a legal conclusion.
